Chapter 3: Lessons from Suffering—Finding Purpose in Pain.
You know, pain has this uncanny way of stripping away all our illusions. When you're facing illness, when your body's fighting and the future feels shaky, all those things that once seemed so important—success, comfort, the need for approval—suddenly, they just don’t matter as much. In those tough moments, a different kind of clarity starts to break through.
I remember my third encounter with death came during a season of deep, personal loss. Hope felt so far away, and every prayer seemed to echo back with silence. The days just blurred together, each one heavy with exhaustion and disappointment.
Friends and family tried to help, and their support did mean something, but honestly, their words often felt empty. The real battle happened when I was alone, just me, my thoughts, and my fears. There were nights when giving up felt like the easier path—when despair was right there, whispering in the darkness.
But even in those darkest hours, there was always this small, persistent voice—just a flicker of hope. It kept suggesting that maybe, just maybe, all this pain wasn’t meaningless.
One night, when the fever was burning and my mind started to drift, something shifted. Instead of traveling somewhere far away, this journey went inward, straight to the heart. Suddenly, memories of past mistakes and regrets started surfacing, each one sharper than the last. The guilt was heavy—almost crushing. But right alongside it, there was this incredible sense of being seen and understood. In that raw, vulnerable state, I could feel the presence of something bigger—a kind of love that didn’t judge, but instead, offered healing.
That’s when it hit me: suffering, as painful as it is, can actually serve a real purpose. The wounds from the past aren’t meant to stay hidden or ignored. They need to be brought into the light, where they can finally start to heal. It’s not an easy process—it takes honesty, and a lot of humility. But as the days went by, this quiet strength started growing in me. Even in weakness, I felt held.
Most of us will do just about anything to avoid pain. We chase comfort, security—anything that’ll keep us safe. But what if it’s the very things we fear the most that push us to grow? That’s what suffering became for me: a teacher. It revealed truths I don’t think I could’ve learned any other way.
Forgiveness, both given and received, suddenly became so important. And I realized how much I needed to let go of pride and self-reliance.
As my health slowly returned, those lessons stuck with me. The scars didn’t disappear, but now, they tell a different story. They remind me of a journey—not just through darkness, but into light. It wasn’t just about surviving. It was about being transformed.
So, here’s the key takeaway: Pain doesn’t have to be wasted. It can become a doorway—to deeper faith, and a clearer sense of purpose.
